issues.legal_issue: A restriction on partition recorded as an agreement in a village settlement remains effective only while that settlement is in force.
material_facts: An agreement restricting partition was recorded in an earlier settlement and repeated in later settlements.
The settlements containing that agreement had expired.
A restriction was entered in the current settlement on the Collector’s orders, without the agreement of the co-sharers against whom it was asserted.
issues.conclusion: The restriction operated only during the settlements in which it was recorded and did not survive their expiry; the later entry made without the co-sharers’ agreement did not make the restriction binding on them.
issues.legal_principle: An entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz is effective during the currency of the settlement in which it is made and becomes inoperative when that settlement ends. The Court relied on Hira v. Muhamadi (16 P.R. 1915 at p. 89), Allah Bakhsh v. Mirza Bashir-ud-Din (1932 L.T.R. 56), and Lieut. Chaudhri Chattar Singh v. Mt. Shugni (A.I.R. 1941 Lah. 239).

rule.if: village_partition_dispute and settlement_recorded_partition_bar and settlement_period_expired and not co_sharer_agreed_to_later_bar

predicates.village_partition_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether co-sharers may partition village property.
predicates.settlement_recorded_partition_bar: An agreement restricting partition was recorded in a settlement record.
predicates.settlement_period_expired: The settlement containing the restriction had ended.
predicates.co_sharer_agreed_to_later_bar: The co-sharer against whom a later restriction is asserted agreed to that restriction.

issues.definition: When a village partition dispute involves a recorded partition bar in an expired settlement and no agreement to a later bar, the expired bar does not restrict partition.

issues.legal_issue: Co-owners may claim partition once their ownership is established and the settlement-based restriction on partition has ceased to operate.
material_facts: A prior judgment between the parties declared the co-sharers’ equal shares and restricted partition only while the relevant Wajib-ul-arz was in force.
Settlement records, including the Khewat, Khatauni, and Jamabandi, recorded the branches as owners in equal shares.
The records and the parties’ conduct supported joint ownership, rather than the claim that the other co-sharers were merely cultivators.
issues.conclusion: The contesting co-sharers were joint owners, and their right to partition could not be resisted after the settlement restriction ceased to operate.
issues.legal_principle: The prior inter partes judgment was res judicata as to the parties’ joint ownership and equal shares. Under sections 31 and 44 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, entries in the record of rights are within the statutory record and are presumed true until the contrary is proved. Partition is a right incident to ownership. The Court also noted section 16 of the earlier Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1871, concerning the presumption attaching to entries made or authenticated at a regular settlement.

predicates.co_ownership_partition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim by co-owners to partition jointly held property.
predicates.co_ownership_established: The parties’ co-ownership of the property has been established by the applicable records, evidence, or a binding prior judgment.
predicates.settlement_partition_bar_expired: The settlement-based restriction on partition has ended.

issues.definition: In a co-ownership partition proceeding, established co-ownership and an expired settlement restriction mean that the co-owners are entitled to partition.

issues.legal_issue: Possession held under an arrangement between co-sharers does not establish adverse possession in the circumstances of the dispute.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed to have acquired title by adverse possession through long possession.
The possession was under an arrangement between the co-sharers.
No issue on adverse possession was framed, no trial-court finding was recorded, and the point was not included in the grounds of appeal to the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The adverse-possession plea had no substance and was rightly rejected because possession under the arrangement between co-sharers did not give rise to adverse possession in these circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that possession under an arrangement between co-sharers, in the circumstances described, does not establish adverse possession. It cited no provision or earlier case for this point.

predicates.coownership_partition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns partition of property held by co-owners.
predicates.adverse_possession_claim_made: A claimant asserts that possession has acquired title by adverse possession.
predicates.possession_under_coowner_arrangement: The possession was held under an arrangement between the co-owners.

issues.definition: In a co-ownership partition proceeding, a claim based on possession held under an arrangement between co-owners does not establish adverse possession.
